review_order: Use whole RGB and structural connections to identify selected pallet; nominal selected-instance wireframe is an uncertain orientation/identity cue only.
Identify the intended native-role outer end structure using dictionary and connected deck/runner/block topology. A visible adjacent board is not automatically the intended end.
Observe intended end-part visibility independently of unchanged query position.
Observe unchanged query relation using exact q96/central32 plus full RGB; reference crop is separate diagnostic only.
Record evidence and unresolved ambiguity; retain every case, including UNKNOWN.

dictionary_check.role_definition: camera-dynamic cuboid role; no fixed physical vertex identity
dictionary_check.rear_order: paired across depth, not independently image-X sorted

selected_instance_criteria.CLEAR: Whole-frame RGB connects the intended end structure to one selected pallet through consistent deck, runner and/or block adjacency and orientation. Similar wood color, nearest pallet or a nominal wireframe overlap alone is insufficient.
selected_instance_criteria.AMBIGUOUS: Two or more plausible pallet instances, stacked pallets, intersecting structures or uncertain nominal alignment prevent unique correspondence.
selected_instance_criteria.NOT_VISUALLY_RESOLVABLE: The selected pallet/required structure cannot be identified from the supplied RGB evidence.

native_part_visibility_criteria.VISIBLE_SUPPORTED: The intended selected-instance outer deck/runner end structure itself has a coherent visible RGB surface/edge witness and supporting structural adjacency; not merely another nearby visible part. Nominal reference need not be pixel-exact and q need not be ON this part.
native_part_visibility_criteria.EXTERNAL_BLOCK_SUPPORTED: The intended end location is supported by adjacent selected-pallet edges continuing behind a distinct foreground object. Nominal reference falling on foreign material alone is insufficient.
native_part_visibility_criteria.SELF_HIDE_SUPPORTED: The intended end identity is structurally supported and the selected pallet's own visible structure demonstrably hides it. Rear role alone, absence of a visible end or a projection on wood is insufficient.
native_part_visibility_criteria.BOUNDARY_OR_GAP_AMBIGUOUS: The relevant end is associated with a visible edge, opening, missing material or mixed boundary, but RGB cannot establish material-end visibility versus gap/virtual cuboid/nominal-pose mismatch.
native_part_visibility_criteria.UNKNOWN: Insufficient RGB support for intended end identity or for distinguishing visibility, external blocking, self hiding and boundary/gap.

query_relation_criteria.ON_INTENDED_PART_SUPPORTED: Unchanged query is visibly on the identified intended end structure. This is coarse structural correspondence, not exact corner or coordinate-quality certification.
query_relation_criteria.NEAR_INTENDED_PART_SAME_SELECTED_PALLET: Query is actually on an immediately adjacent facet of the same selected pallet, with a clear RGB structural relation to the identified intended end. If q is on background/gap, use BACKGROUND_OR_GAP even when a visible intended part is nearby. No numeric distance cutoff.
query_relation_criteria.OTHER_SELECTED_PALLET_PART: Query is visibly on a different identified part of the selected pallet, rather than the intended end neighborhood.
query_relation_criteria.FOREIGN_OBJECT: Query is visibly on a distinct object; this alone says nothing about whether intended native part is visible elsewhere.
query_relation_criteria.BACKGROUND_OR_GAP: Query is visibly on natural floor/wall/background or an actual opening. Padded/invalid samples are not natural background.
query_relation_criteria.UNKNOWN: Query is on an ambiguous/mixed/invalid boundary or the required selected-part relation is unresolved.

consistency_rules: Intended/near/other-selected query categories require CLEAR selected-instance correspondence and an explicit RGB structural reason.

Selected-instance AMBIGUOUS or NOT_VISUALLY_RESOLVABLE prevents supported intended-native visibility; use UNKNOWN or BOUNDARY_OR_GAP_AMBIGUOUS as appropriate, with reason. Literal FOREIGN_OBJECT or BACKGROUND_OR_GAP may still be reported when independently clear.
Visibility and query relation are separate axes: intended part may be visible while q is foreign/background/other part; q can touch selected wood without supporting intended part visibility.
Central samples that are invalid/padded or bilinear mixed must not be called clear background/foreign/material solely from their color; inspect validity and state uncertainty.

WEAK_CANDIDATE_PART_VISIBLE_AND_Q_RELATED only when instance CLEAR, part VISIBLE_SUPPORTED and q ON_INTENDED_PART_SUPPORTED or NEAR_INTENDED_PART_SAME_SELECTED_PALLET. This descriptive flag is not admission.
Optional part_support_extent is a coarse visible structural region, not a new native coordinate, corrected q, physical corner point or <=3px gold.
No native/owner/quality labels overwritten, no training admission, no distance-derived visibility label and no hard pixel/pose/dimension uncertainty bound.
Primary130 and cross40 are separate outputs; all cross40 reviewed without reading other reviewer votes. Preserve overlaps and all UNKNOWN rows.
forbidden_evidence: nominal reference or mask as physical pixel gold
reviewer_context: Reviewers have historical project context; this is evidence-blinded new RGB observation, not naive human annotation or human gold.
